label: Men-at-arms type name
summary: Going by its name, the name of the regiment's men-at-arms type (such as heavy infantry), as plain text without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla never uses it, so this rests on the name alone. A regiment is one unit of men-at-arms, the professional soldiers a ruler recruits and pays for.

label: Name
summary: The name of the men-at-arms regiment.
details: Vanilla puts it into texts about the regiment, for example when a regiment's station is replaced or when a regiment is handed over to another title, and into the interaction window. A separate GetNameNoTooltip exists.

label: Name without tooltip
summary: The name of the men-at-arms regiment, as plain text without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla shows it in the men-at-arms window and in the regiment's tooltip.

label: Origin province
summary: The province the men-at-arms regiment comes from, where it is stationed.
details: Vanilla uses it as the context for parts of the men-at-arms window. The military window shows a part of its layout only while it is not set and the player has domain provinces that could serve as an origin. Texts about replacing a regiment's origin call it the place the regiment is stationed. The game documents no return type.

label: Owner
summary: The character who owns the men-at-arms regiment.
details: Vanilla reads the owner's culture from it to pick the culture's picture for the men-at-arms type, in the men-at-arms window, the siege window and the regiment tooltip. The game documents no return type.

label: Owning title
summary: The title that owns the men-at-arms regiment.
details: Vanilla uses it in the texts about transferring control or ownership to another title for a cost, and as a context in the men-at-arms window. The game documents no return type.

label: Provisions cost text
summary: A text with what the men-at-arms regiment costs in provisions.
details: Vanilla shows it in the men-at-arms window and in the regiment's tooltip; in the tooltip only when the player is a landless adventurer.

label: Total cost text
summary: A text with the total upkeep of the men-at-arms regiment.
details: Vanilla's military view shows it as the regiment's maintenance per month, with the unit 'month' written next to it in the text.

label: Total cost tooltip
summary: Going by its name, the tooltip text that breaks down the regiment's total cost.
details: Vanilla never uses it, so this rests on the name alone. GetTotalCostString gives the total itself.

label: Has reinforcement cost
summary: Going by its name, whether the regiment currently costs extra to bring back up to strength.
details: Vanilla never uses it, so this rests on the name alone. A similar function, CalcReinforcementCost, is what the men-at-arms texts show as the 'Full Maintenance' per month.

label: Is at full strength
summary: Whether the men-at-arms regiment has all its soldiers.
details: The game's name is misspelled ('Stength' without the r) and has to be written that way. Vanilla's men-at-arms window shows a 'Reinforcing' note when the regiment is not at full strength, and 'Raised' or 'Unraised' when it is. The maintenance texts highlight the full maintenance line when the regiment is not at full strength or is raised, and the unraised line when it is at full strength and not raised.

label: Is personal
summary: Going by its name, whether the regiment belongs to the character personally rather than to a title.
details: Vanilla never uses it on a regiment; the lines with the same name are about scheme types and say nothing here. Regiments can also belong to a title (see GetOwningTitle).

label: Is raised
summary: Whether the men-at-arms regiment is raised (the opposite is unraised).
details: Vanilla's men-at-arms window shows 'Raised' for a regiment at full strength that is raised and 'Unraised' for one that is not. The maintenance texts highlight the full maintenance line when the regiment is raised, and the unraised line only when it is at full strength and not raised.

label: Is regular
summary: Whether the regiment is a regular one; vanilla shows the maintenance part of the regiment tooltip only then.
details: The game does not say what makes a regiment not regular. In the tooltip, the block it shows holds the full and unraised maintenance lines.

label: Is open in men-at-arms view
summary: Whether this regiment is the one currently opened in the men-at-arms view of the military window.
details: Vanilla highlights the regiment's entry when it is, and only then hides the button that opens it (which calls ToggleMaaView).

label: Is valid
summary: Going by its name, whether there really is a regiment here.
details: Vanilla never names it on a regiment; on other things IsValid checks that something is set before it is shown, which is only a hint.

label: As script scope
summary: Turns the regiment into a script scope, going by its return type.
details: Vanilla never uses it on a regiment. On other things vanilla uses MakeScope to read script values, for example from the player character, which is only a hint for what it allows here.

label: Regiment itself
summary: The men-at-arms regiment itself.
details: Vanilla passes it as an argument, to select this regiment in an interaction's confirmation window. The game documents no return type.

label: Toggle men-at-arms view
summary: Opens or closes the men-at-arms view for this regiment in the military window.
details: Vanilla calls it when the player clicks the regiment's entry. It is an action for buttons and returns nothing.

label: Access combat stats itself
summary: A function on a regiment's battle results (one row of the battle summary) that, going by its name, hands back the row itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Soldiers at the end
summary: How many soldiers of this regiment were left at the end of the battle.
details: The battle summary shows it as 'left / at the start' next to GetInitialCount, and shows something extra when it is 0, that is, when the regiment was wiped out.

label: Soldiers at the start
summary: How many soldiers this regiment had when the battle began.
details: The battle summary shows it after GetFinalCount, as 'left / at the start'.

label: Knight
summary: The knight this battle-summary row is about, when the row is a knight.
details: Vanilla uses it as the context for the knight's portrait and checks with it whether the knight was killed in the battle. The game documents no return type.

label: Kills in main phase
summary: How many enemy soldiers this regiment killed in the main phase of the battle.
details: Vanilla shows it in the battle summary, with the tooltip 'Kills in the main phase'. The pursuit phase has its own count (GetPursuitKills).

label: Losses in main phase
summary: How many soldiers this regiment lost in the main phase of the battle.
details: Vanilla shows it in the battle summary, with the tooltip 'Losses in the main phase'.

label: Men-at-arms type
summary: The men-at-arms type of this battle-summary row, such as heavy infantry.
details: Vanilla reads the type's name and its culture picture from it in the battle summary. The game documents no return type.

label: Kills in pursuit
summary: How many enemy soldiers this regiment killed in the pursuit phase of the battle.
details: Vanilla shows it in the battle summary, with the tooltip 'Kills in the pursuit phase'.

label: Losses in pursuit
summary: How many soldiers this regiment lost in the pursuit phase of the battle.
details: Vanilla shows it in the battle summary. Its tooltip splits it into men killed by the pursuers (GetPursuitLossesByMaa) and men left behind during the retreat (GetPursuitLossesSelf).

label: Killed by pursuers
summary: How many of this regiment's soldiers the pursuing enemy forces killed in the pursuit phase.
details: Vanilla shows it in the tooltip of the pursuit losses, beside the men left behind during the retreat.

label: Left behind in retreat
summary: How many of this regiment's soldiers were left behind during the retreat in the pursuit phase.
details: Vanilla shows it in the tooltip of the pursuit losses, beside the men killed by the pursuers.

label: Total kills
summary: How many enemy soldiers this regiment killed over the whole battle.
details: Vanilla shows it in the battle summary.

label: Total losses
summary: How many soldiers this regiment lost over the whole battle.
details: Vanilla shows it in the battle summary, with the tooltip 'Total losses'.

label: Is knight
summary: Whether this battle-summary row is a knight rather than a group of soldiers.
details: Vanilla shows the knight's parts of the row only then, and the men-at-arms parts only when the row is neither a knight nor levies.

label: Is levies
summary: Whether this battle-summary row is levies rather than a knight or a men-at-arms regiment.
details: Vanilla shows the levy parts of the row only then, and the men-at-arms parts only when the row is neither levies nor a knight.

label: Is men-at-arms
summary: Whether this battle-summary row is a men-at-arms regiment.
details: Vanilla shows a part of the row only for men-at-arms.

label: Combat stats itself
summary: A function on a regiment's battle results that hands back the row itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. In game texts Self follows other things, for example Character.Self passed as an argument; those lines belong to other types and are only a hint.

label: Access holding bonus itself
summary: A function on a men-at-arms holding bonus (how a men-at-arms type fares in a kind of holding) that, going by its name, hands back the bonus itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Effect text
summary: A text listing what this holding modifier does to the men-at-arms type.
details: Vanilla shows it in a tooltip headed 'In' and the holding's name.

label: Holding type
summary: The kind of holding (such as a castle or a city) this men-at-arms bonus applies in.
details: Vanilla reads its name for the tooltip heading and the icon of its main building for the men-at-arms type view. The game documents no return type.

label: Is positive
summary: Whether this holding modifier helps the men-at-arms type rather than hurting it.
details: Vanilla's men-at-arms type view shows one look for a helpful modifier and another for a harmful one.

label: Holding bonus itself
summary: A function on a men-at-arms holding modifier that hands back the modifier itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. In game texts Self follows other things, for example Character.Self passed as an argument; those lines belong to other types and are only a hint.

label: Access entry itself
summary: A function on an army reorganization entry (one unit in the list for moving troops between armies) that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Coat of arms title
summary: A title whose holder's coat of arms vanilla shows on the entry, when ShowCoA says so.
details: In the army window the element is named for hired troops, so it likely marks whose troops these are; the game does not say which title it is. The game documents no return type.

label: Special troops name
summary: The name of the special troops in this army reorganization entry.
details: Vanilla shows it in a tooltip labelled 'special troops'. The army window ties an icon for event troops to the entry, so these are probably troops added by events, but the game does not say so.

label: Knight
summary: The knight in this army reorganization entry, when the entry is a knight.
details: Vanilla uses it as the context for the knight's portrait. When it is not set and the entry is not men-at-arms, the entry is levies, from the domain or from a vassal. The game documents no return type.

label: Men-at-arms type
summary: The men-at-arms type of this army reorganization entry.
details: Vanilla uses it as a context in the army window, for entries that are men-at-arms. The game documents no return type.

label: Maximum soldiers
summary: The most soldiers this army reorganization entry can hold.
details: Vanilla shows it in the entry's tooltip as the maximum, after the current count from GetSoldierCount.

label: Name
summary: The name of this army reorganization entry.
details: Vanilla shows it as the entry's text in the army window.

label: Regiment
summary: The army regiment behind this reorganization entry.
details: Vanilla reads from it the vassal the levies come from, and the regiment behind it in turn. The game documents no return type.

label: Soldier count
summary: How many soldiers this army reorganization entry has now.
details: Vanilla shows it in the entry's tooltip, before the maximum from GetMaxSoldierCount.

label: Is men-at-arms
summary: Whether this army reorganization entry is a men-at-arms regiment.
details: Vanilla shows a men-at-arms icon then; entries that are neither men-at-arms nor a knight get a levy icon.

label: Move regiment
summary: Moves this entry between the two lists of the army reorganization window.
details: Vanilla calls it when the player clicks an entry in either of the window's two lists. It is an action for buttons and returns nothing.

label: Entry itself
summary: A function on an army reorganization entry that hands back the entry itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. In game texts Self follows other things, for example Character.Self passed as an argument; those lines belong to other types and are only a hint.

label: Shows coat of arms
summary: Whether the entry shows a coat of arms, that of the holder of GetCoATitle.
details: Vanilla uses it on the element named for hired troops in the army window.

label: Access terrain bonus itself
summary: A function on a men-at-arms terrain modifier (how a men-at-arms type fares in a kind of terrain) that, going by its name, hands back the modifier itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Effect text
summary: A text listing what this terrain modifier does to the men-at-arms type.
details: Vanilla shows it in a tooltip headed 'In' and the terrain's name.

label: Terrain
summary: The terrain (such as hills or desert) this men-at-arms modifier applies in.
details: Vanilla reads its name for the tooltip heading and its icon for the men-at-arms type view. The game documents no return type.

label: Is positive
summary: Whether this terrain modifier helps the men-at-arms type rather than hurting it.
details: Vanilla's men-at-arms type view shows one look for a helpful modifier and another for a harmful one.

label: Terrain bonus itself
summary: A function on a men-at-arms terrain modifier that hands back the modifier itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. In game texts Self follows other things, for example Character.Self passed as an argument; those lines belong to other types and are only a hint.

label: Access winter modifier itself
summary: A function on a men-at-arms winter modifier (how a men-at-arms type fares in winter) that, going by its name, hands back the modifier itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Effect text
summary: Going by its name, a text listing what this winter modifier does to the men-at-arms type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. A tooltip 'In Normal Winter' shows the same function after MenAtArmsType.GetWinterNormalModifier, which probably gives this type, but the game does not say so.

label: Is positive
summary: Going by its name, whether this winter modifier helps the men-at-arms type rather than hurting it.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. The men-at-arms type view uses the same name after MenAtArmsType.GetWinterHarshModifier, which probably gives this type, but the game does not say so.

label: Winter modifier itself
summary: A function on a men-at-arms winter modifier that hands back the modifier itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. In game texts Self follows other things, for example Character.Self passed as an argument; those lines belong to other types and are only a hint.

label: Access religion itself
summary: A function on a religion (a group of related faiths, such as Christianity) that, going by its name, hands back the religion itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Custom text
summary: Going by its name, the text of a custom localization entry worked out for this religion; it takes the entry's key.
details: Vanilla never uses it on a religion. On characters vanilla writes Character.Custom('key') to pull in a custom localization (text the game picks from several options by script conditions); that is a hint for how it works here.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the custom localization entry, going by the use on other types.

label: Adherent name
summary: The word for one follower of the religion, such as 'Muslim'.
details: Decision texts use it on a religion looked up by its key, for example to say that vassals of that religion cannot join certain factions. Variants without tooltip and in the plural also exist.

label: Adherent name, no tooltip
summary: Going by its name, the word for one follower of the religion, as plain text without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; the lines with the same name are on faiths, which have their own adherent names. GetAdherentName gives the word with its tooltip.

label: Adherents' name
summary: The word for the followers of the religion in the plural, such as 'Muslims'.
details: A decision text uses it on a religion looked up by its key ("... are more likely to accept conversion"). A variant without tooltip, GetAdherentNamePluralNoTooltip, also exists.

label: Adherents' name, no tooltip
summary: The word for the followers of the religion in the plural, as plain text without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in the ledger, for example in 'All' followers of the religion and in the line on how many holy sites they control, and in legend texts.

label: Adjective
summary: The religion's adjective, such as 'Christian' in 'Christian Relic'.
details: Vanilla texts use it on religions looked up by their key, for example to name relics. A variant without tooltip, GetAdjectiveNoTooltip, also exists.

label: Adjective, no tooltip
summary: The adjective of the religion, as plain text without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in the faith view's filter 'Only [adjective] faiths' and in ledger tooltips such as the religion's rulers, sinful rulers and virtuous rulers.

label: Change in counties
summary: How many counties the religion will gain overall, or lose when the number is negative, through the conversions now going on.
details: It is the counties being converted to the religion minus its counties being converted away (see GetCountiesGain and GetCountiesLoss). Vanilla shows it in the ledger with a plus or minus sign, and its tooltip says 'gain' or 'lose' by its sign.

label: Counties being gained
summary: How many counties are being converted to this religion right now.
details: Vanilla shows it in the ledger tooltip of the change in counties.

label: Counties being lost
summary: How many of the religion's counties are being converted to another religion right now.
details: Vanilla shows it in the ledger tooltip of the change in counties.

label: Faiths
summary: The list of faiths that belong to the religion.
details: Vanilla's ledger fills a list with them, checks whether there are any, and reacts when there is exactly one. The game documents no return type.

label: Religion family
summary: The family the religion belongs to, such as Abrahamic or Pagan.
details: Vanilla shows the family's name in brackets after the religion's name, and in the ledger without a tooltip because the Pagan one is very long, as a comment in the file says.

label: Flavor description
summary: The descriptive flavor text of the religion.
details: Vanilla shows it in the religion's tooltip.

label: Name
summary: The name of the religion, such as Christianity.
details: Vanilla shows it in the ledger and in the explanation of how a religion weighs a trait. A variant without tooltip, GetNameNoTooltip, also exists.

label: Name without tooltip
summary: The name of the religion, as plain text without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in legend texts, on a religion stored on the legend, and in ledger tooltips.

label: Controlled holy sites
summary: How many of the religion's holy sites are held by its own followers.
details: Vanilla's ledger shows it as 'controlled / all', next to GetNumberOfHolySites.

label: Number of counties
summary: How many counties follow the religion.
details: Vanilla shows it in the ledger.

label: Number of followers
summary: How many followers the religion has.
details: Vanilla shows it in the ledger, with the tooltip 'All' and the plural name of its followers.

label: Number of holy sites
summary: How many holy sites the religion has in all.
details: Vanilla's ledger shows it after the number its followers control (GetNumberOfControlledHolySites).

label: Number of holy wars
summary: How many holy wars the religion is fighting right now, going by its name and its war icon in the ledger.
details: Vanilla shows it in the ledger with a war icon, only when it is not zero. The game does not say whether wars against it count too.

label: Number of rulers
summary: How many rulers follow the religion.
details: Vanilla shows it in the ledger with the tooltip of the religion's rulers, and shows the counts of sinful and virtuous rulers only when it is not zero.

label: Number of sinful rulers
summary: How many sinful rulers the religion has.
details: Vanilla shows it in the ledger, with the tooltip 'Sinful' and the religion's adjective and 'rulers'. The game does not say in the files read what makes a ruler sinful.

label: Number of virtuous rulers
summary: How many virtuous rulers the religion has.
details: Vanilla shows it in the ledger, with the tooltip 'Virtuous' and the religion's adjective and 'rulers'. The game does not say in the files read what makes a ruler virtuous.

label: Total military strength
summary: The total soldiers of all rulers of the religion.
details: Vanilla shows it in the ledger, shortened for large numbers; its tooltip reads 'Total soldiers of all' rulers of the religion. The game does not say how it is added up.

label: Religion definition
summary: The definition behind the religion, from which vanilla reads its description of virtues and sins.
details: Vanilla uses it in the religion's tooltip to show which traits count as virtues and sins (ReligionType.GetVirtuesSinsDescription). The game documents no return type.

label: Has pagan roots
summary: Going by its name, whether the religion has pagan roots.
details: Vanilla never names it on a religion directly, but the faith tooltip uses it on a faith's religion (Faith.GetReligion.HasPaganRoots) together with whether the faith is unreformed, to choose between two texts. What exactly counts as pagan roots is not shown.

label: As script scope
summary: The religion as a general script object, so it can be compared with or passed to other functions.
details: Decision texts use it to check whether a character's faith belongs to a religion looked up by its key: they compare the faith's religion with this result and pick the text to show from that.

label: Religion itself
summary: The religion itself.
details: Vanilla passes it as an argument, to pin or unpin the religion in the ledger, to check whether it is pinned, and to get its list of faiths in the ruler designer. The game documents no return type.

label: Access family itself
summary: A function on a religion family (a group of religions, such as Abrahamic) that, going by its name, hands back the family itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Name
summary: The name of the religion family, such as Abrahamic.
details: Vanilla uses it after Religion.GetFamily, to show the family in brackets after a religion's name. A variant without tooltip, GetNameNoTooltip, also exists.

label: Name without tooltip
summary: The name of the religion family, as plain text without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in the family's tooltip, as in 'The following religions are' the family name, and as the heading of that tooltip.

label: Religions list
summary: A text listing the religions that belong to the family.
details: Vanilla puts it in the family's tooltip after 'The following religions are' the family name. It returns text, not a list to loop over.

label: Hostility description
summary: A text describing how hostile the family's faiths are to faiths of other families, going by its name.
details: Vanilla puts it at the top of the family's tooltip, before the list of the family's religions. What the text says is not shown in the game files.

label: Family itself
summary: A function on a religion family that hands back the family itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. In game texts Self follows other things, for example Character.Self passed as an argument; those lines belong to other types and are only a hint.

label: Access definition itself
summary: A function on a religion definition (what Religion.GetType gives) that, going by its name, hands back the definition itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Most eminent holy sites
summary: Going by its name, the most eminent holy sites a faith of this religion may have.
details: Vanilla reaches it through a faith's religion (faith.GetReligion.GetType) in the reason text of the decision to elevate a holy site: the faith must have fewer eminent holy sites than this.

label: Fewest eminent holy sites
summary: Going by its name, the fewest eminent holy sites a faith of this religion may have.
details: Vanilla reaches it through a faith's religion (faith.GetReligion.GetType) in the reason text of the decision to demote a holy site: the faith must have more eminent holy sites than this.

label: Most holy sites
summary: Going by its name, the most holy sites a faith of this religion may have.
details: Vanilla reaches it through a faith's religion (faith.GetReligion.GetType) in the reason text of the decision to adopt a holy site: the faith must have fewer holy sites than this.

label: Fewest holy sites
summary: Going by its name, the fewest holy sites a faith of this religion may have.
details: Vanilla reaches it through a faith's religion (faith.GetReligion.GetType) in the reason text of the decision to abandon a holy site: the faith must have more holy sites than this.

label: Index
summary: Going by its name, the number the game uses internally for this religion definition.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; the lines with the same name are on legitimacy types and say nothing here.

label: Key
summary: Going by its name, the script key of the religion, such as christianity_religion.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; on buildings and other things GetKey gives the script key, which is only a hint.

label: Log name
summary: A function on a religion definition that, going by its name, gives the name used in the game's logs.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Main holy site
summary: A function on a religion definition that, going by its name, gives its main holy site.
details: Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents no return type.

label: Name
summary: Going by its name, the name of the religion this definition is for.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; the lines with the same name belong to other types.

label: Virtues and sins text
summary: A text describing which traits the religion counts as virtues and which as sins.
details: Vanilla reaches it through Religion.GetType and shows it in the religion's tooltip.

label: Is valid
summary: Going by its name, whether there really is a religion definition here.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; on other things IsValid checks that something is set, which is only a hint.

label: Localized text
summary: Going by its name, a translated text for the religion definition; it takes one argument.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type, so what the argument is is not shown. The lines with the same name use a global Localize that turns a key into text, which is only a hint.

label: Definition itself
summary: A function on a religion definition that hands back the definition itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. In game texts Self follows other things, for example Character.Self passed as an argument; those lines belong to other types and are only a hint.

label: Access religion window itself
summary: A function on the religion window (the window listing a religion's faiths) that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Close
summary: Closes the religion window.
details: Vanilla calls it from the window's close buttons. It is an action for buttons and returns nothing.

label: Faiths
summary: The list of faiths the religion window shows.
details: Vanilla fills the window's faith list with it. The game documents no return type.

label: Sort options
summary: The list of ways the religion window can sort its faiths.
details: Vanilla fills the window's sort drop-down with it. The game documents no return type.

label: Selected sort option
summary: Which sort option of the religion window is selected right now.
details: Vanilla uses it as the selected entry of the sort drop-down. Its type is a pair of whole numbers.

label: Religion
summary: The religion the religion window is showing.
details: Vanilla uses it as the context for the window's contents. The game documents no return type.

label: Filter tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the religion window's filter that shows only this religion's faiths.
details: Vanilla uses it on that filter's checkbox. The faith view's texts for this filter read 'Show Only' and the religion's adjective followed by 'faiths'.

label: Sort order
summary: Whether the religion window sorts its faiths in ascending order; false means descending.
details: Vanilla shows 'Ascending' or 'Descending' by it in the sort button's tooltip, and picks the button's picture by it.

label: Is visible
summary: Whether the religion window is open.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the window.

label: Sort option changed
summary: Applies the sort option the player picked in the religion window's drop-down.
details: Vanilla calls it when the drop-down's selection changes. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle religion filter
summary: Switches the religion window's filter that shows only this religion's faiths on or off.
details: Vanilla calls it when the player clicks the filter's checkbox; ShowOnlyReligionFaiths tells whether it is on. It returns nothing.

label: Reverse sort order
summary: Flips the religion window's sort order between ascending and descending.
details: Vanilla calls it from the sort order button, whose tooltip says 'Click to toggle'. It returns nothing.

label: Religion window itself
summary: A function on the religion window that hands back the window itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. In game texts Self follows other things, for example Character.Self passed as an argument; those lines belong to other types and are only a hint.

label: Shows only religion's faiths
summary: Whether the religion window's filter that shows only this religion's faiths is on.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of the filter's checkbox.

label: Toggle
summary: Going by its name, opens the religion window when it is closed and closes it when it is open.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; the lines with the same word are texts, not uses. It returns nothing.

label: Access map icon itself
summary: A function on a religious head map icon (the map marker of a head of faith or rite) that, going by its name, hands back the icon itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Character
summary: The religious head this map icon stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the context of the whole icon, which then shows the character's faith. The game documents no return type.

label: Is head of faith
summary: Whether the map icon's character is the head of a faith; otherwise it is only the head of a rite.
details: Vanilla shows the faith's icon on the map for a head of faith and a rite icon for a head of rite.

label: Map icon itself
summary: A function on a religious head map icon that hands back the icon itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. In game texts Self follows other things, for example Character.Self passed as an argument; those lines belong to other types and are only a hint.

label: Access window itself
summary: A function on the remove-friend confirmation window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: The game lists this window among its interface types, but vanilla never uses it; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Confirm removal
summary: Confirms removing a friend in the engine's remove-friend confirmation window; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the window's YES button; CANCEL closes the window with Hide instead.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the engine's remove-friend confirmation window without removing anyone; it returns nothing.
details: The window's close button and its CANCEL button call it.

label: Window itself
summary: A function on the remove-friend confirmation window that hands back the window itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. In game texts Self follows other things, for example Character.Self passed as an argument; those lines belong to other types and are only a hint.

label: Should be shown
summary: Whether the engine's remove-friend confirmation window should be on screen (yes or no).
details: The window is visible only while this is true.

label: Show
summary: Going by its name, opens the remove-friend confirmation window.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; the lines with the same word are texts, not uses. It returns nothing.

label: Access rename popup itself
summary: A function on the rename popup (the dialog where the player types a new name) that, going by its name, hands back the popup itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Color
summary: The color currently picked in the rename popup's color picker.
details: Some renames also let the player choose a color; vanilla shows that part only when UsesColor is true. It returns a color value.

label: Color label
summary: The label shown above the rename popup's color picker.
details: Vanilla shows it only in the color part of the popup.

label: Rename popup itself
summary: A function on the rename popup that hands back the popup itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. In game texts Self follows other things, for example Character.Self passed as an argument; those lines belong to other types and are only a hint.

label: Set color
summary: Stores the color the player picks in the rename popup's color picker.
details: Vanilla calls it each time the color in the picker is changed. It returns nothing.

label: Uses color
summary: Whether this rename also lets the player pick a color.
details: Vanilla shows the popup's color label and color picker only then.

label: Uses two text fields
summary: Whether the rename popup asks for two texts instead of one.
details: Vanilla shows a single text box when it is false and a pair of boxes when it is true. The game does not say which renames need two.

label: Access repack window itself
summary: A function on the repack window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type. Nothing in the base game's own files explains what the repack window is.

label: Current tile size
summary: The heightmap's current tile size, as a whole number.
details: The map editor's repack heightmap window shows it as "Tile size (currently ...)" above the tile size choices (33, 65 or 129).

label: Repack heightmap
summary: Repacks the map's heightmap with the chosen settings; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the Repack button in the map editor's repack window. The window warns that repacking overwrites manual resolution changes.

label: Repack window itself
summary: A function on the repack window that hands back the window itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. In game texts Self follows other things, for example Character.Self passed as an argument; those lines belong to other types and are only a hint.

label: Set tile size
summary: Chooses the tile size to repack the heightmap with; it returns nothing.
details: The repack window's tile size checkboxes call it with 33, 65 or 129; 33 is checked at the start.

label: Wrap X
summary: Whether the heightmap repack wraps along the X axis (left to right) (yes or no).
details: The repack window's Wrap X checkbox shows this value; ToggleShouldWrapX switches it. Going by the name, it joins the map's left and right edges; the game does not say more.
